verdict.rationale: WezTerm's docs state it runs on Linux, macOS and Windows 10, and it uses a single Lua config file (.wezterm.lua in the home directory, or next to wezterm.exe for portable setups). Community users report keeping one config across Linux, macOS and Windows machines. Missing for 10: first-party documentation that the same config works unchanged across OSes, and one user notes only 'large parts' of the config are shared, implying some per-OS adjustments.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the same terminal with the same config on macOS, Linux, and Windows

citations.quote: Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows 10, FreeBSD and NetBSD
A GPU-accelerated cross-platform terminal emulator and multiplexer
Create a file named `.wezterm.lua` in your home directory
wezterm will look for the config file in the same location as wezterm.exe
They work across Linux, macOS and Windows, learn one terminal, and share large parts of the config between OSes.
Keeps a single WezTerm config, wraps it in a nix expression for home-manager/NixOS, and symlinks it on Windows as a portal to WSL.
